data_limitation: Raw document texts are not individually accessible (SQLite tables empty; Q-files contain aggregated tag data only). Outcome counts are derived from recovery subcategory tags and explicit quote-level resolution signals. The dominant 'Outcome Not Stated' bucket is an honest finding, not a classification failure.

outcomes.label: First-Attempt Success
outcomes.description: User's initial query succeeded; no refinement or fallback needed.
outcomes.derivation: Zero by corpus construction — Bucket A contains friction/failure documents. A user whose first search succeeded would not write a critical review.

outcomes.label: Success After Refinement
outcomes.description: User rephrased/iterated the search (within the search feature, including Ask Photos) and eventually found the photo.
outcomes.derivation: Zero from available aggregate data. No Q-file quotes contain within-search-iteration success language. 4 docs describe competitor_switch (Apple Photos/Immich) which is platform abandonment, not within-Google-Photos refinement success.

outcomes.label: Success via Fallback
outcomes.description: User abandoned search entirely and found the photo through manual timeline scrolling, WhatsApp, or asking someone — after failing search.
outcomes.derivation: 1 doc confirmed by explicit resolution quote in q10.json: 'I was scrolling through things and eventually found them, and I cannot remember the date for the life of me.' (Reddit, confidence 0.95).
outcomes.evidence_quote: I was scrolling through things and eventually found them, and I cannot remember the date for the life of me.

outcomes.label: Abandonment
outcomes.description: User gave up with no resolution — described a dead end with no path forward.
outcomes.derivation: Derived from strong dead-end signals in bucket_a_findings.json recovery subcategories: no_refinement_support (11 docs) + gemini_conversation_dead_end (9 docs) + cold_restart_each_try (1 docs) = 21 docs.

outcomes.label: Outcome Not Stated
outcomes.description: Document describes the friction/failure but does not narrate what ultimately happened. The user is venting about the problem, not reporting a resolution.
outcomes.derivation: Remainder after allocating: 251 total - 0 first-success - 0 after-refinement - 1 via-fallback - 21 abandonment = 229. This includes 177 docs with no recovery tag at all (Expression/Interpretation/Evaluation failures where no resolution was narrated) plus 51 fallback_to_scroll docs minus the 1 confirmed success and 21 confirmed abandonment, plus 2 other_recovery docs.

cross_reference_with_failure_type_table: The failure-type table (Section 4.0.1) shows 51 docs with fallback behavior. The outcome table shows only 1 confirmed success via fallback and 21 abandonment. The remaining 29 scroll docs land in 'Outcome Not Stated' — they describe the scrolling behavior but do not narrate whether the photo was found. This is consistent, not contradictory: failure-type captures WHERE it broke, outcome captures WHAT ULTIMATELY HAPPENED. The low confirmed-success rate from fallback suggests that even the 51 docs describing scrolling mostly did not self-rescue successfully — they vented about the necessity of scrolling without confirming they found the photo.
key_finding: 91.2% (229/251) of Bucket A documents do not state an outcome — the corpus is composed of friction-venting reviews, not resolution narratives. This is itself a product insight: the magnitude of unresolved frustration is invisible from outcome data alone; it requires reading the failure-type signals.
